core_claim: Innovation earns temporary rents that attract imitators and new innovators, who make old products and firms obsolete.
business_use: Scanning for innovations that could make a whole category unnecessary

core_claim: Incumbents win sustaining innovation but lose to entrants that start in low-end or new-market footholds and improve until good enough for the mainstream.
business_use: Deciding whether and how to respond to low-cost or simpler entrants

core_claim: Whether innovators or imitators capture value depends on the appropriability regime, the dominant design, and control of complementary assets.
business_use: Build, partner, or license decisions for new technologies

core_claim: Reconfiguring links among existing components destroys architectural knowledge that incumbents embed in their communication channels and information filters.
business_use: Diagnosing blind spots in product development organizations

core_claim: Industries move from an era of ferment to a dominant design, after which innovation shifts from product to process and firms shake out.
business_use: Timing entry and investment across the technology cycle

core_claim: Firms gain from purposive inflows and outflows of knowledge, but returns to external search breadth diminish and eventually turn negative.
business_use: Designing partnership, licensing, and external sourcing portfolios

core_claim: Under uncertainty, expert entrepreneurs start from available means, limit losses to what is affordable, and let goals emerge from stakeholder commitments.
business_use: Early-stage venture design and internal venturing

core_claim: Opportunities are either discovered by alert individuals with relevant prior knowledge or created through entrepreneurs' own actions under uncertainty.
business_use: Choosing between planning and iterative approaches to new markets

core_claim: Resource-constrained entrepreneurs create value by recombining resources at hand and refusing to accept conventional limits on their use.
business_use: Frugal innovation and growth of resource-constrained ventures

core_claim: Young organizations fail at higher rates because roles, trust, routines, external ties, and legitimacy take time to develop.
business_use: Staging venture funding and support for young firms
